newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada sees stock offer, assets sale.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada sees stock offer, assets sale.

text.p: Oil company Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Wednesday it planned an offering of its stock and a flotation of its Indonesian unit next year to help fund its proposed acquisition of Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc.
Chief executive J.P. Bryan said the firm had arranged a credit line with banks to fund the planned 432 million stg buy, adding that it had yet to meet with Clyde to discuss the deal.
Bryan told reporters on a conference call that the company planned to raise about $100 million from an offering of its stock in the U.S. and Canada early next year.

Gulf Canada also planned to sell some $300 million in non-strategic assets throughout 1997, assuming its acquisition of Clyde was successful. In addition, the company planned to float about 20 percent of its Indonesian unit, Asamera, late next year to raise $300 to $400 million, Bryan said.
He said Clyde had an attractive portfolio of producing properties, adding that the British firm's assets in Australia and Indonesia would complement Gulf Canada's own operations in those countries.
"We have stated publicly that we wanted to put a so-called third leg on the stool, which is another area of influence for Gulf outside Canada and Indonesia," Bryan said.
He said Gulf Canada would not have to pay an "exploration premium" for Clyde, adding that the UK firm had not had very good results on the exploration side recently.

Cost-savings were not a significant incentive behind the bid, he said. "What we see is good production and good cash flow. On a cash flow basis, this is accretive to Gulf shareholders. It's not dilutive," Bryan said.
Gulf's offer represented about a 20 percent premium over Clyde's asset value, according to its calculations.
"We certainly think we're paying a full price, but we don't think we're overpaying for it," he said.
"We would hope that the management (of Clyde) would concur with us and recommend this favourably. We've tried to reach them -- at this point unsuccessfully," he added.
Bryan said the company had looked at other takeover targets, but he did not give names.
"It's safe to say that Gulf has examined almost every exploration and production company in the United States, Australia and the UK in the past 18 months," he said.
He added that the Clyde deal, if successful, would fulfil the company's immediate acquisition goals.
"Our commitment over the next few years would be to try to add significant value to the assets we already have," he said.
Regarding Gulf's Indonesian assets, Bryan said the company expected gas projects coming on stream there in 1998/99 to generate $200 to $300 million in annual net cash flow for it.
The deals included its partnership in the Corridor project and its agreement to supply Mobil Corp's Arun LNG plant.
Bryan added that Gulf also expected to receive some 400 million barrels of oil equivalent from its about 50-percent stake in a recent gas exploration discovery in Indonesia.
He declined to forecast Gulf Canada's earnings.
"We can tell you that volumes and cash flow will continue to improve in this company," he said.
-- Jeff Daeschner, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
